GKFlasher is an open source Python project supported by OpenGK, written by dante383 and dmg210. This project is a multi OBD2 tool for the Siemens ECUs found on the Hyundai and Kia vehicles. It can read & write tune data, correct EEPROM checksums and clear adaptive values from your ECU. 

== MSI Install Package ==
We have precompiled MSI install packages available from the GitHub releases page:

https://github.com/Dante383/GKFlasher/releases

=== Prerequisites ===
'''1)''' First you will need a FTDI USB-OBD2 interface cable. This is often the same cable used on German vehicles. The chipset on the board must be a real FTDI chip and cannot be one of the CH340C chips. Through extensive testing we found that the following cable is the least expensive and most reliable cable for GKFlasher:

[https://www.aliexpress.us/item/2251832612703671.html Galletto 1260 ECU Chip Tuning Tool EOBD Programmer FTDI] Note: These adapters are not currently supported with BSL.   

Pictured here shows the good FTDI chipset and the CH340C chipsets.

[[File:FTDI Example.png|269x269px]]:[[File:CH340C Example.png]]

<nowiki>*</nowiki>from GKFlasher v1.0.5 we have added support for the CH340 chipset. 

== Manual Windows 10 & 11 Installation ==
If you'd like to participate in the development of GKFlasher the guide below will demonstrate how to download, install and configure all the prerequisites for GKFlasher. If you are a GitHub user, please go star the following repository:

https://github.com/Dante383/GKFlasher

'''1)''' Download the following files: 

[https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/releases/download/v2.44.0.windows.1/Git-2.44.0-64-bit.exe Git-2.44.0-64-bit.exe]

[https://www.python.org/ftp/python/3.11.9/python-3.11.9-amd64.exe python-3.11.9-amd64.exe]

''Optional download for npcap if you are using a CAN BUS interface for a specific purpose:''

[https://npcap.com/dist/npcap-1.79.exe npcap-1.79.exe]

=== Install GIT & Python ===
'''3)''' Open the Git install file named <u>Git-2.44.0-64-bit.exe</u> selecting "Git from the command line" from the following screen, then continue with all the default options afterwards:

[[File:Git Install 1.png|border]]

'''4)''' Open the Python installation file named <u>python-3.11.9-amd64.exe</u> and on the first dialogue select "Add python.exe to PATH"

[[File:Python Install 1.png]]

Keep all the default values on the following screen:

[[File:Python Install 2.png]]

Select "Install Pyhon 3.11 for all users" from the following screen: '''"Add Python to environment variables" has to be selected!'''

[[File:Python Install 3.png]]

'''5)''' Once installation is complete you may need to logout of windows or restart your computer before the Powershell will recognize the new PATH entries for GIT and Python. To test if either program works, try the following commands after the '''>''' symbol in Windows Powershell and you should see the following responses if all is well. If you do not see these responses or receive a "ObjectNotFound" type of error, then try the above installations again.
 PS C:\Users\cfham> '''python -V'''
 Python 3.11.9

 PS C:\Users\cfham> '''git.exe -v'''
 git version 2.44.0.windows.1

=== NPCAP Install (Optional) ===
'''1)''' If you are using CANBUS for your read/write functions, open and install the file named <u>npcap-1.79.exe</u> using default options.

[[File:GKFlasher First Time.png|701x701px]]

'''5) Optional:''' Create a desktop shortcut to open GKFlasher easily. First we'll need to know the location of your python3.11.exe executable. Execute the following command from your Powershell or command prompt and enter the command after the '''>''' symbol. The following line you will use to copy/paste into your desktop shortcut. In this example it is located in my local user's directory within a subfolder. Yours will vary depending on your username.
 PS C:\GIT Repos\GKFlasher> '''(Get-Command python.exe).Path'''
 C:\Users\cfham\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\python.exe
Right click on your desktop and go to "New" and "Shortcut", then paste the line you found from the last Powershell command and click next:

[[File:GKFlasher Desktop Shortcut 1.png]]

[[File:GKFlasher Desktop Shortcut 2.png|border]]

Type in "GKFlasher" into the next window and press Finish:

[[File:GKFlasher Desktop Shortcut 3.png|border]]

Now right click on that new shortcut and select properties. You will change a couple of settings in this new window so that it starts the GKFlasher app and change to the correct starting directory. First add " gui.py" (Contains a space) to the end of the target prompt and copy/paste the directory location you chose for your GIT Repos containing GKFlasher and press apply. The following is using my example directory. Yours may be unique.

[[File:GKFlasher Desktop Shortcut 4.png|border]]

If you would like to add an icon to your shortcut, you can download the OpenGK/GKFlasher logo from [https://opengk.org/files/Users/chase206/Siemens_T_Logo.ico Siemens_T_Logo.ico] and add it to your GKFLasher shortcut using the "Change Icon" button.

== Manual Ubuntu & Mint 22.3 Installation ==

=== Pre-requisites ===
From a fresh installation of Ubuntu 24.04 or Mint 22.3 you will need to install GIT and Python-PIP:
 nobody@mintgkflasher:~$ sudo apt-get install git python3-pip

=== GIT Clone & PIP Requirements.txt ===
Download GKFlasher from GIT and run the PIP Requirements command:
 nobody@mintgkflasher:~$ git clone https://github.com/Dante383/GKFlasher.git
 nobody@mintgkflasher:~$ cd GKFlasher
 nobody@mintgkflasher:~GKFlasher$ python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt --break-system-packages
If all is well you can now run the gui.py file from the GKFLasher directory:
 nobody@mintgkflasher:~GKFlasher$ python3 gui.py
